relevance_note: Original report of HA20 describing identifiable TNFAIP3 carriers, e.g. "an affected mother (P4) and daughter (P6)" sharing "a novel variant in TNFAIP3".
method_note: Written by hand with a small Python builder script (all values from my reading). The paper's Supplementary Table 1 (clinical details) and pedigree figures are not in the Markdown, so per-person phenotypes are sparse. Table 1 is per family (rows are families): its variant was attached to each family member the text ties to that family. Family 1 = affected mother + two affected daughters (labels by rules 6 and 2; the paper gives them no labels in the text). Families 3, 4, 5: one index patient each was recorded (unnamed persons 5-7); the number of affected members per family is not given in the text (pedigrees only in Fig. 1a). Family 6 = the adult-onset Behcet's case (unnamed person 8) and her two affected daughters; Family 6 is linked to her by the identical variant p.Pro268Leufs*19 in Table 1 and the text. Family 2's three unaffected Sanger-sequenced members (unnamed persons 2-4) are recorded without variant rows: the text says only that the variant 'segregated', not that they tested negative. Family 1's 'maternal unaffected family members' were Sanger sequenced but their number is not given, so no rows. P9 is named only in Fig. 2d (p65 nuclear fraction assay); family and variant are not stated, so no variant row; P9 may be one of the unlabelled people above (possible duplicate). The 'affected sister of P6' (Fig. 1a legend) was not studied: no variant row. Table 1 'Inheritance' column says 'De novo' for Family 4 but no parental testing is described, so inheritance is 'not reported' (rule 8); 'Dominant' is a mode of inheritance, not origin. Family 1 daughters: maternal carrier status is not stated explicitly, so inheritance not reported. Zygosity 'heterozygous' comes from the abstract's statement about the six families (all carriers belong to them). The general statement 'The identified mutations were considered pathogenic' was not used for pathogenicity (v5). Variant type is only from sentences naming the exact variant (Family 6 frameshift); 'nonsense and frameshift variants' for Families 3-5 is a list of values, not used. Family 1's features ('early-onset systemic inflammation, arthralgia/arthritis, oral/genital ulcers and ocular inflammation') describe the family, not named individuals, so they were not assigned to any member. 'oral/genital ulcers' shared by P4, P5, P6 was read as both oral and genital ulcers on the checklist (ambiguous slash). Group exclusions: 'none of our patients have developed lymphomas or other malignancies' and 'an overt autoimmune disease was only diagnosed in Patient 6' were applied to all study patients (not to the unstudied sister or unaffected relatives); neither excludes any narrower checklist item. Anakinra 'normalized markers of systemic inflammation in Patient 6' was not recorded as elevated markers (implied, not stated). Five patients 'developed autoantibodies' is a count without names. n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated left null: Methods give 7 (NIH) + 4 (Utrecht) + 2 (Hacettepe) evaluated patients but no single stated total. No contradictions found apart from Family 2 ancestry ('Italian ancestry' in text vs 'European American' in Table 1), both recorded.
